activities.caption: true or false — what 'sterile' commits you to
activities.name: stAbsJudge

statements.s: A tray processed correctly can be 99.9% sterile.
statements.why: Sterile means free of all microbial life, including spores — a tray is either sterile or contaminated.

statements.s: Because contamination is invisible, the field runs on process rather than inspection.
statements.why: You cannot see bacteria on a drape — the point is maintaining conditions under which invisible organisms had no opportunity to arrive.

statements.s: Asepsis is chiefly about removing visible dirt.
statements.why: That is cleanliness, a lower level of purity — asepsis targets microbial contamination, which is invisible.

activities.caption: you spot a doubt — walk the arithmetic
activities.name: stDoubtBranch

config.root: A doubt about sterility just crossed your hands. Walk the logic.

start.text: A small tear in a wrapper on the back table. What now?

choices.label: Announce it and pull the item
choices.feedback: A torn wrapper is an event — the barrier is breached whether or not anything got in.

choices.label: Check whether the instrument inside looks clean
choices.feedback: Contamination is invisible — inspection cannot clear it.

looks.text: The instrument looks spotless. Now what?

choices.label: Still pull it — the event happened
choices.feedback: Sterility is event-related: the torn wrapper ended the guarantee.

choices.label: Use it — spotless is spotless
choices.feedback: A spotless-but-unsterile instrument is far more dangerous than the reverse.

safe.text: Discarded and replaced. The downside of tossing a doubtless-fine pack is minutes and currency; the reflex is arithmetic, not rigidity.

risk.text: Dead end — the downside of keeping a contaminated one is a surgical site infection, among the most common and most preventable complications. Never test the patient's blood with a debate.

config.why: When in doubt, throw it out — the logic leaves no alternative.

activities.caption: knowing the enemy — pair each player with its fact
activities.name: stOrgMatch

config.prompt: Match each organism or reservoir to its fact:

pairs.right: resident flora in follicles and glands, where antiseptic scrubs cannot fully reach
the densest bacterial concentration in nature — why bowel surgery is intrinsically the highest infection risk

config.why: The air adds dust-borne bacteria and fungal spores, and transient organisms ride on everything touched — the cast that makes surgery a controlled invasion.

activities.caption: every rule blocks a route — file the countermeasure
activities.name: stRouteSort

config.prompt: Which route does each countermeasure block?
config.why: Skin flora travel by contact, spores settle from above, instruments carry previous handling, and fluids carry bloodborne viruses — every aseptic rule maps onto one of these routes.

activities.anchor: Two microbiological facts deserve special attention
activities.caption: one line of the spore brief is wrong — click it
activities.name: stSporeSpot

config.prompt: One line of this spore brief is wrong — click it:
lines: Spores are the dormant, armoured forms of certain bacteria.
They survive boiling, drying and years of waiting.
Boiling water kills them, which is why boiled instruments count as sterile.
Only sterilisation-grade heat or chemicals kill spores — which is why spores are the benchmark every sterilisation process is tested against.
Biofilms sealed in self-made slime resist disinfectants and the body's defences, so dried blood and tissue must be cleaned off before sterilisation.
config.correction: Boiling does not kill spores — that is exactly why only sterilisation-grade heat or chemicals qualify, and why boiled is not sterile.
config.why: Dried residue can shield organisms inside a biofilm from the process itself: the sterilant kills only what it can reach.

config.prompt: Pressurised steam in the autoclave — roughly how hot does it run, in °C?
config.why: Roughly 121–134 °C — steam transfers heat far faster than dry air, denaturing proteins and killing spores in minutes. Heat-sensitive cameras and light cables get low-temperature oxidative chemistry at 45–55 °C instead.
config.context: Ethylene oxide penetrates beautifully and kills thoroughly but is toxic and flammable, demanding long aeration.

activities.anchor: walking it end to end is the best exercise
activities.caption: case cart to back table — rebuild the opening sequence
activities.name: stCycleOrder

config.prompt: Before the case — order the opening sequence:
items: The case cart arrives with wrapped, indicator-checked trays selected from the surgeon's preference card
The scrub verifies external indicators and integrator status, and checks pack integrity
Open each item onto the back table in a fixed order: basins, then linen, then instruments
Wrappers fold outward without touching sterile surfaces
Sharps are counted, and blades are loaded with an instrument — never fingers
config.why: Every step is one place asepsis can fail — which is why the cycle is taught as a single unbroken chain rather than a list of chores.

activities.anchor: geometry must be memorised as reflexes
activities.caption: the sterile zone is a shape — file each surface
activities.name: stZoneSort

config.prompt: Sterile or unsterile? File each surface:

items.label: the gowned front, chest to sterile-gloved hands
the back, shoulders and sides of any gowned person
a border of about 2.5 cm around a sterile drape's edge

config.why: The drape border counts as unsterile because objects can touch it from below without anyone seeing — which is why scrubbed people pass back-to-back and nothing is ever reached over.
